location: Washington, D.C. and Little Rock, AR
description: Congressman French Hill (AR02) has internship positions available for the Fall 2025 term in both his DC and Little Rock offices. Interns will work in a fast-paced environment, gaining valuable exposure and knowledge of the legislative process and the U.S. Congress while helping central Arkansans. Intern responsibilities include answering constituent phone calls, assisting staff with administrative tasks, conducting legislative research, and assisting with correspondence. Interns should have a positive attitude, strong work ethic, and excellent written and oral communication skills. Successful interns will be detail-oriented self-starters, take and listen to direction, and be willing to work both independently and as part of a team. Applicants should have a working knowledge of current events and policy topics as well as a willingness to assist with daily office tasks. Arkansas ties strongly preferred. Internships are open to college and graduate students as well as recent graduates. The office offers paid and unpaid internships depending on availability.
qualifications: Positive attitude and strong work ethic
Excellent written and oral communication skills
Ability to take and listen to direction
Willingness to work both independently and as part of a team
Working knowledge of current events and policy topics
Willingness to assist with daily office tasks
Open to college and graduate students as well as recent graduates
how_to_apply: Send a resume and cover letter to AR02.Applications@mail.house.gov indicating which location you are applying for. Applications should be submitted by June 30 but will be accepted on a rolling basis until all positions are filled.

description: Congresswoman Suzan DelBene, representing the 1st Congressional District of Washington state, seeks interns for her Washington, D.C. and District offices. Interns will work in a fast-paced congressional office, gaining valuable experience and knowledge of the United States Congress. Congressional internships are open to all majors and designed for undergraduate and graduate students, as well as recent graduates with an interest in public service. Starting and ending dates are flexible, although prospective interns should be able to commit to at least 17 hours per week during the internship. A stipend of $1,000/month will be provided to full-time interns and a stipend of $500/month will be provided to part-time interns. The deadline for Fall 2025 Internship Applications is 11:59 PM on Sunday, July 6, 2025. Due to a high volume of applications, you may only be contacted if you are selected for an interview.
responsibilities: Greeting constituents and handling constituent phone calls
Kirkland, WA interns: attending community events and tours with the Congresswoman and staff
Washington, D.C. interns: leading tours of the U.S. Capitol and attending hearings and briefings for the legislative staff
qualifications: Exceptional written and oral communication skills
A strong interest in public service
Washington state ties are a plus but are not required
Open to all majors; designed for undergraduate and graduate students, as well as recent graduates
Ability to commit to at least 17 hours per week
how_to_apply: Submit a cover letter, resume, and short writing sample (1 to 2 pages) through the online form. The deadline for Fall 2025 Internship Applications is 11:59 PM on Sunday, July 6, 2025. No phone calls or walk ins.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status.

description: The office of U.S. Congressman Jeff Van Drew (Republican-NJ-02) is currently accepting applications for his Washington, D.C. office for full and part-time interns for the fall internship session. This is a conservative office, so each intern will be required to express the Congressman's conservative perspective to constituents and people who call into the office. The start date would be as early as August 6th (flexible depending on availability) with a flexible end date. Interns are paid a stipend based on availability and have access to transit benefits. The internship will offer students and young professionals invaluable experience with our nation's legislative process. Interns contribute to the daily operations of the office and are expected to act in a reliable, professional manner at all times. Congressman Van Drew supports students requesting credit for their internship through their university.
responsibilities: Various other tasks to assist staff
Expressing the Congressman's conservative perspective to constituents and callers
qualifications: Must act in a reliable, professional manner at all times
Ability to express the Congressman's conservative perspective to constituents and callers
Available for full or part-time internship starting as early as August 6th
how_to_apply: Email a resume and cover letter to nj02internships@mail.house.gov. Indicate in your cover letter that you are applying for a fall internship and format the files as [Full Name_Resume], [Full Name_Cover Letter].
